questions.idea: Is there a multi-dimensional refusal CONE in audio language models, and is its dimensionality conserved with the vision-language cone?
questions.note: Greenfield (agent-synthesized, red-gap): P135/P136 recover only a single audio refusal direction while P152 measured a refusal-cone dimensionality in vision-language; nobody has asked whether audio carries a cone of comparable dimensionality.

questions.idea: Does the refusal non-uniqueness / cone-count result (RQ24) hold for non-refusal behaviors such as truth, sycophancy and persona?
questions.note: Greenfield (agent-synthesized, red-gap): refusal counting/non-uniqueness (P18/P19/P137) has no analogue for the non-refusal behaviors that only have single directions (P77 traits, P84 truth, P88 traits, P153 sycophancy).

questions.idea: Is refusal in diffusion language models a multi-dimensional cone evolving across denoising steps, not a single per-step signal?
questions.note: Greenfield (agent-synthesized, red-gap): P118 (step-wise SRI), P128 (jailbreak) and P129 (trajectory re-mask) treat diffusion refusal as a single signal; the cone view (P17/P18 for dense) is unasked there.

questions.idea: Is the mixture-of-experts refusal mechanism a per-expert cone concentrated in safety experts, or distributed across routing?
questions.note: Greenfield (agent-synthesized, red-gap): P80/P113 find 'safety experts' and positional concentration and P114 asks routing-vs-within-expert at the neuron level, but the per-expert refusal CONE/dimensionality is unasked.

questions.idea: Is there ONE shared cross-modal refusal vector validated jointly across audio, vision and video, rather than a separate direction recovered per modality?
questions.note: Greenfield (agent-synthesized, cross-paper): P135/P136 (audio 'golden' vector), P101/P131 (modality shift / video), P152 (VLM cone) each work one modality at a time; the unified cross-modal object is unasked.

questions.idea: Across dense, mixture-of-experts, state-space and diffusion models, is refusal carried by the SAME geometric object (direction/cone) or is it architecture-specific?
questions.note: Greenfield (agent-synthesized, cross-paper): P132/P35 (SSM), P80/P114 (MoE), P118/P128 (diffusion) each characterise refusal within one architecture; the cross-architecture invariance question is unasked.

questions.idea: Can a latent refusal-direction monitor be built that provably survives ADAPTIVE evasion, not just one adaptive attacker?
questions.note: Greenfield (agent-synthesized, cross-paper): P38 evades probes (recall 100%->0%) and P85 is the first monitor against an adaptive attacker, while P103 reads refusal linearly pre-generation; a certified adaptive-robust latent monitor is unasked.

questions.idea: Does a nonlinear / manifold refusal geometry transfer cone-to-cone ACROSS models, not just within one model?
questions.note: Greenfield (agent-synthesized, cross-paper): P132 (affine concept editing), P144 (manifold) and P145 (invertible steering) show nonlinear paths WITHIN a model; cross-model nonlinear transfer is unasked.

questions.idea: Do the shared LLM<->vision-language safety neurons imply a shared cross-modal refusal SUBSPACE whose ablation transfers across modalities?
questions.note: Greenfield (agent-synthesized, cross-paper): P102 finds >50% shared top safety neurons LLM<->VLM and P152 a VLM cone; whether a single shared subspace governs both, and whether ablating it transfers, is unasked.

questions.idea: Can the step-wise internal refusal signal in diffusion LMs be reinforced across denoising to resist trajectory re-masking attacks?
questions.note: Greenfield (agent-synthesized, cross-paper): P118 exposes a step-wise refusal signal that P128/P129 defeat by re-masking committed refusals; a denoising-time defense that reinforces the signal is unasked.

questions.idea: extend prompt-level jailbreaking to multi-turn conversations
questions.quote: Directions for future work include extending this framework to systematically generate red teaming datasets for fine-tuning to improve the safety of LLMs and extending to multi-turn conversations.
questions.note: Realized by: P10 (Crescendo, a multi-turn escalation jailbreak that gradually escalates a benign dialogue into a successful jailbreak).

questions.idea: turn the pre-decoding refusal probe into a defense: early jailbreak detection, adversarial training, principled layer selection
questions.quote: Future work should investigate defensive uses of these signals, including early jailbreak detection, adversarial training, and more principled layer selection.

questions.idea: extend the steering-vector / refusal-overlap analysis to a higher-dimensional refusal subspace
questions.quote: Therefore, a valuable direction for future work would be to extend our analysis to a higher-dimensional refusal subspace.

questions.idea: apply the steering-vector safety audit to OTHER steering paradigms to test the generality of the refusal-overlap mechanism
questions.quote: A valuable next step for future work would be to apply this security audit to other steering paradigms to confirm the generality of this mechanism.

questions.idea: improve safety evaluators to separate refusal surface form from the actual refused content (audio LALM)
questions.quote: Improving the nuanced capability of safety evaluators (i.e., separating refusal surface form from the actual content) is a promising direction for future work.

questions.idea: predict steerability from richer vector diagnostics / non-linear relationships (vector-separation metrics fail to predict steering success)
questions.quote: Future work should explore whether more sophisticated vector diagnostics or non-linear relationships might better predict steerability.

questions.idea: extend generation-trajectory safety alignment to stochastic decoding and diverse injection sequences
questions.quote: Extending to stochastic decoding is a promising direction.

questions.idea: investigate complex (multi-condition) backdoor trigger conditions, not just complex backdoored behaviors
questions.quote: We choose to focus on the possibility of complex behaviors in the backdoored policy rather than the possibility of complex triggers for the backdoored policy—we leave investigation into complex backdoor trigger conditions for future work.

questions.idea: verify causal necessity of the trigger-hijacked language heads by ablating the identified heads
questions.quote: Verifying causal necessity by ablating the identified heads remains future work.

questions.idea: intervene on persona representations DURING pretraining itself rather than post-hoc
questions.quote: Our findings on the early formation and persistence of persona vectors through alignment open several avenues for future work: characterizing what aspects of pretraining data shape persona formation, intervening on persona representations during pretraining itself rather than after, and extending this analysis to traits beyond the four studied here.

questions.idea: a mechanistic account of WHY safety-intervention timing during pretraining changes robustness
questions.quote: While our experiments establish that intervention timing significantly affects outcomes, understanding the underlying mechanisms remains an open question.

questions.idea: tailored, architecture-specific safety alignment for diffusion LLMs
questions.quote: , even this early attempt significantly boosts rejection of malicious prompts, hinting that robust safety alignment for dLLMs is not only possible but calls for tailored, architecture-specific strategies.

questions.idea: extend affine concept editing beyond refusal to broader (non-refusal) behavior-modification tasks
questions.quote: Future work should explore whether nonlinear approaches could further improve ACE's standardization effect and expand its applicability to broader behavior-modification tasks.

targets: new-axis:reliable composition of multiple simultaneous steering interventions (no tensor axis captures multi-vector composition)
questions.idea: reliable compositionality of multiple steering interventions remains an open challenge
questions.quote: Although many steering methods exploit linear structure that supports additive composition, reliable compositionality remains an open challenge.

targets: new-axis:cross-behavior entanglement / interference between steering targets (no tensor axis captures one steered behavior degrading another)
questions.idea: the mechanisms underlying cross-behavior entanglement of representation steering remain unclear
questions.quote: The mechanisms underlying this entanglement remain unclear and warrant further investigation.

targets: new-axis:conditional-steering thresholds that generalize across prompt distributions (robustness of the steering trigger rather than a tensor cell)
questions.idea: conditional-steering thresholds that generalize across diverse prompt distributions
questions.quote: Future work should explore methods for setting conditional thresholds that generalize across diverse prompt distributions.

targets: new-axis:cross-behavior mechanistic relation between two behaviors (the tensor places one BEHAVIOR per cell and cannot encode a relation between behaviors such as sycophancy and honesty/deception)
questions.idea: the mechanistic relation between sycophantic agreement and honesty/deception is an open question
questions.quote: At the same time, the relation between sycophantic agreement and broader constructs such as honesty and deception remains an open mechanistic question (Marks and Tegmark, 2024).

questions.idea: whether qualitatively different refusal / non-compliance forms rely on DISTINCT underlying mechanisms
questions.quote: This raises a critical open question: do qualitatively different forms of refusal—and more general non-compliance behaviors—rely on distinct underlying mechanisms?

questions.idea: whether harmfulness-feature suppression is the ONLY jailbreak mechanism or other mechanisms exist
questions.quote: Hence, harmfulness feature suppression may not be the only mechanism for jailbreak success, which warrants further research.

questions.idea: whether the attention-hijacking mechanism generalizes to other model TYPES and other attack types
questions.quote: While transformers are widely used, future research may examine whether the hijacking phenomenon generalizes to other model types.

questions.idea: deepen safety alignment via control-theory and safe-reinforcement-learning training approaches
questions.quote: Future work can explore additional approaches grounded in control theory and safe reinforcement learning.

questions.idea: a systematic analysis of the mid-stream prefill attack vector that elicits long harmful continuations
questions.quote: The procedure is unusually potent—capable of eliciting long, high-utility harmful continuations (often > 3,000 tokens) from models such as GPT-4.1/5—and a systematic analysis of this attack vector is deferred to future work.

questions.idea: train chat-model SAEs and extend feature search to attention/MLP for more causal and minimal refusal feature sets
questions.quote: We believe that this can be improved by prioritizing efforts towards training SAEs on chat-model activations, and consider this to be a promising direction for future research.

targets: new-axis:semantic decomposition of refusal drivers (legal reasoning vs moral heuristics) - the tensor has no axis for what semantically drives a refusal decision
questions.idea: to what extent refusal is driven by legal reasoning versus moral heuristics
questions.quote: We hope that our findings inspire deeper mechanistic investigations into LLM refusal and lead to principled audits of LLM safety, enabling answers to questions such as: "To what extent is refusal driven by legal reasoning?" or "How much do moral heuristics contribute to refusal decisions?".

questions.idea: reliable multi-feature / conditional SAE steering and layer-targeting without capability degradation
questions.quote: Determining optimal multi-feature steering approaches is a promising direction for future work.

questions.idea: train models to be easier to robustly monitor (monitorability as a training objective against obfuscated activations)
questions.quote: Training models to be easier to robustly monitor appears to be a promising direction, but not at present a complete solution to obfuscated activations.

questions.idea: use targeted latent adversarial training to harden models against few-shot harmful fine-tuning attacks
questions.quote: We are interested in future work to explore LAT's potential to improve on existing approaches for making models robust to few-shot fine-tuning attacks.

questions.idea: whether multi-layer refusal-direction-fingerprint detection is robust to obfuscation-style attacks beyond GCG suffixes
questions.quote: Whether this distinction provides robustness against obfuscation-style attacks beyond GCG-style suffix optimization is an open question.

questions.idea: train activation probes on model OUTPUTS rather than only on inputs
questions.quote: In this work, we only study input monitoring techniques, although we note that training probes on model outputs is an important future direction.

questions.idea: whether a misaligned model can adversarially subvert the activation probes monitoring it
questions.quote: Relatedly, misaligned AI systems might also be interested in subverting such probes; exploring this adversarial dynamic could be a direction for future work.

questions.idea: design robust jailbreak attacks that cannot be cheaply defended by randomized smoothing
questions.quote: In this way, future research must seek "robust attacks" which cannot cheaply be defended by randomized algorithms like SmoothLLM.

questions.idea: HOW safety neurons exert their influence on safety behavior, not just which neurons matter
questions.quote: Finally, we identified which neurons affect model safety but not how they exert this influence, which will be a future research direction.

questions.idea: incorporate closed-form concept scrubbing into the pretraining and/or finetuning process
questions.quote: If these experiments succeed, an exciting next step would be the incorporation of concept scrubbing into the pretraining and/or finetuning process.

questions.idea: evaluate SYSTEM-level defenses (not just model-level) for automated red-teaming
questions.quote: We focus our large-scale comparison on model-level defenses, although future work could use HarmBench for evaluating system-level defenses.

questions.idea: relate exaggerated-safety/false-refusal to lying, sycophancy and inaccurate self-explanation
questions.quote: These anecdotal results could be explored further in relation to work on detecting when LLMs "lie", sycophancy, or inaccurate self-explanation.

questions.idea: a more granular scoring rubric for safety-refusal evaluation (beyond binary refuse/comply)
questions.quote: While some prior work have taken the first step to conduct safety evaluation under a more granular scoring rubric, we leave this as an important future step.

questions.idea: stronger protective measures against fine-tuning attacks that degrade safety
questions.quote: This study underscores the vulnerabilities in current LLM defenses and highlights the urgent need for further research on enhancing protective measures against fine-tuning attacks.

questions.idea: design training methods that enhance the separation of harmful and harmless content in the embedding space
questions.quote: While our work points to the promise of methods that enhance the separation of harmful and harmless content in the model's embedding space, designing, implementing and testing such methods remains an important direction for future work.

targets: new-axis:the detect-route-generate routing stage between concept detection and behavioral policy that no tensor axis isolates (censorship can hide as narrative steering rather than refusal)
questions.idea: evaluation methods that can detect censorship hidden as narrative steering rather than overt refusal
questions.quote: Building evaluation methods that can see through that invisibility is the next step.

questions.idea: study trajectories manifolds and state-spaces of representations beyond linear subspaces
questions.quote: While we mainly analyzed subspaces of representations, future work could investigate trajectories, manifolds, and state-spaces of representations.

questions.idea: robustly verify the mechanisms properties and effects of activation steering across models and behavior types
questions.quote: Although activation engineering techniques have shown some promise as a way to steer models' behavior, their mechanisms, properties, and effects have yet to be robustly verified across different models and types of behaviors.

questions.idea: whether emergent misalignment can be intentionally induced via a backdoor data-poisoning attack
questions.quote: It's also possible that emergent misalignment could be induced intentionally by bad actors via a backdoor data poisoning attack — although the viability of such attacks is a question for future work.

questions.idea: more convenient and effective realignment mechanisms to reverse emergent misalignment
questions.quote: More convenient and effective realignment mechanisms, however, remain to be developed.

questions.idea: whether alignment gating generalizes to broader categories of model misalignment
questions.quote: Future work can further investigate the applicability of alignment gating and its potential for misalignment mitigation in broader categories of model misalignment.

questions.idea: whether persona behavioral clusters are genuinely distinct model states or artifacts of how the persona axis is constructed
questions.quote: More broadly, it remains open whether these behavioral clusters reflect genuinely distinct persona states in the model, or are artifacts of how we construct the persona axis.

questions.idea: characterize the routing-gate bypass across multi-turn attack strategies
questions.quote: A full characterization across encoding families and multi-turn strategies is left for future work.

questions.idea: a principled combinatorial approach for composing multiple expert-specific steering vectors
questions.quote: We suspect that naively combining two independent steering vectors may be responsible for the poor performance of this intervention, and a more complete combinatorial approach may produce better results, but leave this for future work.

questions.idea: whether shared-representation jailbreak transfer extends to vision-language RAG and mixture-of-experts models
questions.quote: Future work should study whether our findings transfer to other modalities and architectures, such as vision-language models, retrieval-augmented generation, and mixtures-of-experts.

questions.idea: transferability of NONLINEAR refusal probes across model families
questions.quote: Future research should explore the transferability of nonlinear refusal probes across model families and examine their interplay with jailbreak attacks and other adversarial strategies.

questions.idea: circuit-trace the attention heads that carry the multi-turn adversarial-restlessness signal
questions.quote: Future work should localize contributing attention heads via circuit tracing.

questions.idea: next-generation defenses that reason about safety dynamically during inference against closed-loop reasoning attacks
questions.quote: Current defenses remain vulnerable to internally-steered, closed-loop reasoning trajectories under the tested settings, highlighting a critical need for next-generation defenses capable of reasoning about safety dynamically during inference.

questions.idea: treat causal control as a NECESSARY condition for mechanistic claims rather than an optional extension
questions.quote: The finding motivates treating causal control as a necessary condition for mechanistic claims rather than an optional extension.

questions.idea: understand the uniform reasoning strategy and whether it can be steered toward genuinely mode-specific reasoning
questions.quote: Understanding what that uniform strategy is, and whether it can be steered toward genuinely mode-specific reasoning, remains an important open question for the logical reasoning community.

questions.idea: report probe-steering intervention results alongside R^2, treating probe accuracy as necessary but insufficient
questions.quote: We recommend that future work using probes for steering report intervention results alongside R^2, treating probe accuracy as a necessary but insufficient condition.

questions.idea: rigorous wholesale training-time alternatives to post-hoc repair of models already capable of generating harmful content
questions.quote: Historical precedent suggests that we should consider rigorous wholesale alternatives to current attempts, which aim at posthoc "repair" of underlying models that are already capable of generating harmful content.

questions.idea: extend optimization-based jailbreaking to multi-turn settings
questions.quote: For future work, we will explore extensions to multi-turn and multimodal settings, and investigate how our analysis can guide the design of defense strategies.

questions.idea: viability of the exponentiated-gradient attack in black-box scenarios
questions.quote: Its viability in black-box scenarios is left as a direction for future research.

questions.idea: train a classifier specifically for identifying refusal messages in responses
questions.quote: We leave training a classifier specifically for identifying refusal messages in responses to future work.

questions.idea: use the attacker framework to systematically generate red-teaming datasets for safety fine-tuning
questions.quote: Directions for future work include extending this framework to systematically generate red teaming datasets for fine-tuning to improve the safety of LLMs.

questions.idea: evaluate refusal-probe robustness across interdependently constructed datasets and refusal taxonomies
questions.quote: Future work should evaluate probe robustness across interdependently constructed datasets and refusal taxonomies.

questions.idea: understand the nature of chain-of-thought and distilled chain-of-thought backdoored (deceptive) models
questions.quote: We invite future work to help us better understand the nature of chain-of-thought and distilled chain-of-thought backdoored models.

questions.idea: finer-grained per-category, layer-by-layer optimization of which subspace to intervene on
questions.quote: We focus on shared interaction regimes rather than category-specific, layer-by-layer analysis, leaving finer-grained layer optimization to future work.

questions.idea: investigate harmfulness probes and other representation-reading methods alongside circuit-breaking
questions.quote: Further investigation into Harmfulness Probes and other representation reading methods is left for future work.

questions.idea: investigate the internal white-box mechanisms underlying false refusal / exaggerated safety
questions.quote: Investigating the internal mechanisms of white-box models related to false refusal / exaggerated safety constitutes an interesting direction for future research.
